method_note: Read the whole target file. Picked claims by risk: repository metadata (gh api), release tags, EIP/CAIP/IPFS/W3C statuses and ids, EBSI endpoints and encodings, EU law article references (read in the Publications Office cellar texts), DOI titles/years/venues (Crossref and OpenAlex), and existing_check names (compared with docs/reference/capabilities.md and architecture.md section 8). Crossref returned HTTP 429 for one DOI; OpenAlex was used for others. No live endpoint was called; no protected standard was opened. Only 7 of 40 DOIs were re-checked; the other DOIs are unverified by this pass.

checked.claim: ERC-4906 requires MetadataUpdate or BatchMetadataUpdate when token JSON metadata changes; ERC-721 allows a mutable URI
checked.evidence: ERC-4906 requires emission when the JSON metadata changes and advises against it when only the tokenURI changes while the JSON stays the same. ERC-721 rationale says the URI may be mutable. Nuance for an oracle: a URI change with identical JSON does not need the event.
checked.correction: Add the nuance: the event is tied to a change of the JSON metadata, not to a change of the URI string alone.

checked.claim: EBSI guide shows the anchored SHA-256 hash wrapped in a multihash and encoded as multibase base64url with prefix u; timestampId is that encoding of the multihash of SHA-256 of the hash; scope 'openid timestamp:write'; paths /v1/timestamp/timestamps/{id} and /records/{id}[/versions[/{vid}]]; eth_sendRawTransaction; four write methods
checked.evidence: Scope, four read paths, four method names and eth_sendRawTransaction are confirmed. The timestampId derivation (base64url multibase, prefix u, multihash of SHA-256 of the original hash) is confirmed. However the guide's response example returns the stored hash with prefix m (standard base64), and the guide does not document the multihash header bytes. So the statements that the receipt hash is 'sha2-256 code 0x12, length 0x20, prefix u' (conformance_implications[0] fixtures, last failure_mode) are only proven for timestampId, not for the stored hash field.
checked.correction: Limit the u-prefix multihash claim to timestampId; record that the hash field in the response example uses prefix m; mark header bytes 0x12 0x20 as an inference, not a page statement. Fixtures that use a 'wrong prefix' variant need the real field-level encoding first.

checked.evidence: Read the original OJ text: all listed paragraph and point subjects match, including 10(1)(a)-(g), the back-up copy in paragraph 4, 11(a)-(h), the 19 July 2026 date, and 13(5)/(6). Recital 41 says a decentralised data system set up and managed by economic operators plus a Commission registry.

Annex 3(a) lists ETSI EN 319 401 v3.1.1 (2024-06); 3(b)(1) lists ISO 23257:2022 (reference architecture) and 3(b)(2) lists ISO/TS 23635:2022 (governance). This resolves the target's statement that the mapping to point 3(b) was not confirmed.

checked.evidence: The chunk read covered only Art. 36(7)-(11): presumption of conformity for vendors that meet common specifications, harmonised standards, and Member State objections. Art. 36(1)-(5) sub-points were not reached. The vendor presumption through common specifications is present, so 'presumption via harmonised standards' alone in the sources entry is incomplete.

checked.claim: identifier.consistency with compare_item compares the passport with the document behind tokenURI
checked.evidence: The check exists and compare_item compares the resolved passport with the document at the IXIT 'item' template target. The tokenURI document is only that target if the profile sets it as the item template; the check does not read a ledger. The file's own text allows this only for HTTPS targets, which is reasonable but not automatic.

rule5_findings.problem: Minor: the file says the annex adds 'DLT reference-architecture and governance references'. This describes the role of two ISO documents, though the wording comes from EU law (Implementing Regulation 2025/2531 Annex 3(b)), not from the ISO texts.
rule5_findings.fix: Phrase it as 'Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2531 Annex point 3(b) names ISO 23257:2022 and ISO/TS 23635:2022', and cite the regulation, with no description of the ISO content.

rule5_findings.problem: No rule 5 breach: EN 18216/18219-18223/18239/18246 appear only as bibliographic entries with titles used as layer labels. Note that titles are 'prior record' values and urls say 'not re-retrieved'.
rule5_findings.fix: None required. Optionally mark the EN titles as unverified in this session.

missed_items.fact: The create-timestamp guide derives recordId by ABI-encoding owner address, block number and first-version hash, hashing with SHA-256 and encoding the first 32 bytes as multibase base64url. The guide's wording is brief. An oracle for record anchors would depend on this.

A single Proof of Inclusion proof can only cover targets from one transaction; the verifier is intentionally offline and the caller must decide which committee to trust. This limits use as a batch-anchor verifier and makes the pinned-root step an explicit trust decision.

Annex 3(a) lists ETSI EN 319 401 v3.1.1 for all providers; 3(b) lists ISO 23257:2022 (reference architecture) and ISO/TS 23635:2022 (governance) for providers using distributed ledger technology. Numbers only; the standards were not opened.

missed_items.topic: eIDAS 2 mutual recognition of qualified ledgers
missed_items.fact: Article 24a(11) of the amended Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 says a qualified electronic ledger provided in one Member State is recognised in all other Member States.
A smart contract vendor is presumed conformant if it meets common specifications (Art. 36(9)); harmonised standards in the OJ replace overlapping common specifications (36(10)).

overall: The target file is mostly reliable on what could be re-checked: all 12 repository records (licence, archived flag, last push, release tags), the EIP and CAIP statuses and interface ids, W3C DID 1.1, the IOTA and did:ebsi syntax, the EBSI Track and Trace access check, and the EU law citations (ESPR Arts 9-13, eIDAS 2 Arts 45k and 45l, Implementing Regulation 2025/2531) matched primary sources. Errors found: the IPFS gateway precedence of the format parameter is overstated (SHOULD, not MUST), the bcra DOI year is 2022 where Crossref gives 2023, and the EBSI multibase 'u' encoding is proven only for timestampId, not for the stored hash field (the guide shows prefix m there). Some claims could not be confirmed: Data Act Art. 36(1)-(5), the PurgePrivateData behaviour, and the use of compare_item for a tokenURI document. Only 7 of the 40 DOIs and a subset of the claims were re-checked, and the EDPB content, registry Implementing Regulation 2026/1778 and the literature abstracts were not re-verified. Rule 5 hygiene is good; the EN, ISO and ETSI entries are bibliographic, with one minor wording risk around ISO 23257 and ISO/TS 23635.
